selection_process: Preliminary Examination: Held at various centres in the districts of U.P. to select candidates for the Main (Written) Examination. Objective type

with negative marking. Main (Written) Examination: Only candidates declared successful in the Preliminary Examination are admitted. Candidates must fill a fresh application form and pay the Main Examination fee

and must appear against the same Roll No. allotted for the Preliminary Examination. Selection is made on the basis of total marks obtained in the Main (Written) Examination. Document verification and medical examination: Candidates must submit a hard copy of their online application with self-attested copies of marksheets and certificates when asked. Selected candidates must undergo a medical examination as required under the Rules.
On the basis of the Preliminary Examination result

candidates equal to fifteen times the number of vacancies are declared successful for the Main Examination. Minimum efficiency standard: 35% for SC and ST candidates and 40% for candidates of other categories in the Preliminary/Main Examination. Candidates scoring below this are treated as disqualified. Candidates serving under the Central or State Government must produce a 'No Objection Certificate' from their employer
issued by the competent authority. An interview or personality test is not mentioned in the provided notification.

pattern_table.Paper Name: One third (0.33) of the marks assigned to the question for each wrong answer. More than one answer is treated as wrong. No penalty for a blank answer.

pattern_table.Subject and Pattern: General Studies-I, traditional type. 20 questions: 10 short-answer questions (8 marks each, 75 words) and 10 long-answer questions (12 marks each, 125 words)
General Studies-II, traditional type. 20 questions: 10 short-answer (8 marks each, 75 words) and 10 long-answer (12 marks each, 125 words)
General Hindi and Writing, traditional type. 8 questions, some with internal options. Marks for each question are shown against it in the syllabus.
Hindi Essay, traditional type. Two essays: first essay 80 marks (800 words) and second essay 120 marks (1200 words)

exam_pattern.details: General Studies (Objective Type): 1. General Science, 2. History of India, 3. Indian National Movement, 4. Indian Polity, Economy and Culture, 5. Indian Agriculture, Commerce and Trade, 6. Population, Ecology and Urbanisation (in Indian context), 7. World Geography and Geography and Natural Resources of India, 8. Current National and International Important Events, 9. General Intelligentsia, 10. Special Knowledge regarding Education, Culture, Agriculture, Industry, Trade, Living and Social Traditions of Uttar Pradesh. | General Hindi (Objective Type): (1) Opposites (10 words), (2) Sentences and Correction in framing (10 sentences), (3) One word for several words (10 words), (4) Same uses and same nature words (10 words), (5) A Noun as defined by an adjective and an adjective (10 words), (6) Synonymous words (10 words). | Paper-1, General Studies-I: | Indian History, Art and Culture: Indian Culture (art forms, literature and architecture from ancient to modern times); Modern Indian history (1757 to 1947): significant events and personalities; the Freedom Struggle; post-independence consolidation and reorganisation within the country (till 1965). Indian Society: Salient features of Indian society and culture; role of women, population and associated issues, urbanisation; liberalisation, privatisation and globalisation and their effects on social structure; social empowerment, social justice and inclusive growth. Geography of India: Physical, Economic and Human Geography of India; Geography of Uttar Pradesh (physical, human and economic aspects, and contemporary issues related to planning and development). Environment and Disaster Management: Environment concept, ecosystems, cycles and biosphere; man-environment relationship, pollution, degradation, conservation and Environment Protection Act; nature and types of disasters; disaster management cycle (Preparation, Rescue, Relief and Rebuilding), role of NDMA, NDRF and SDRF. Science and Technology: Developments and applications of science and technology in everyday life; India's science and technology policy; satellite communication, remote sensing, GPS, space technologies; IT industry, telecommunication; missile systems, UAVs, stealth technology, chemical and biological weapons; nanoscience and nanotechnology; robotics and artificial intelligence; nuclear power policy, nuclear energy applications, radiation, radioactive waste; biotechnology and microbiology, biopiracy, bioinformatics and ethical dimension in biotechnology. | Paper-2, General Studies-II: | Indian Polity and Constitution: Historical underpinnings, evolution, features, amendments, significant provisions and basic structure of the Constitution; role of the Supreme Court; functions and responsibilities of the Union and the States, federal structure, devolution of powers and finances up to local levels; role of the Finance Commission in Centre-State financial relations; Parliament and State legislatures. Governance: Structure, organisation and functioning of the Executive and the Judiciary; pressure groups; Public Interest Litigation (PIL); appointment to Constitutional posts; statutory, regulatory and quasi-judicial bodies including NITI Aayog; Government policies and interventions for development and Information Communication Technology (ICT). Economy and Agriculture: Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), manufacturing sector, energy scenario, means of transport; Government Budget and financial system, effects of liberalisation and globalisation, industrial policies, foreign trade; production of major crops, commercialisation of agriculture, manures, fertilizers, irrigation, storage, transportation and marketing of agricultural produce, e-technology for farmers; farm subsidies and minimum support prices, agricultural diversity, problems of agriculture in U.P., technology missions in agriculture. Ethics and Integrity: Ethics foundations and characteristics; ethical thoughts (Rit and Dharma, Purushartha, Yama, Niyama, Brahma-viharas, Utilitarianism, Deontological theory, Emotivism); attitude; aptitude and emotional intelligence. Current Affairs: Current affairs of regional, national and international importance including games and sports: Global, South Asia and SAARC, India, and Uttar Pradesh. | The Ethics and Integrity and Current Affairs topics appear under the label "Paper-IV" in the printed syllabus on page 8. Candidates should confirm their paper placement in the official PDF. | Paper-3, General Hindi and Writing (marks as printed): | Title of an unseen prose passage, explanation of three underlined parts and summary (5+15+10 = 30 marks) Summary of a given government letter in tabular form (10 marks); correspondence: official letter, semi-official letter, office order, circular, reminder, office memorandum, notification, noting and report (10+10 = 20 marks) Technical terminology (administrative and commercial): Hindi to English and English to Hindi translation (10+10 = 20 marks) Idioms and proverbs: meaning and use in sentences, only ten (10x3 = 30 marks) Grammar: noun, pronoun, adjective, case, verb (5x3 = 15 marks); punctuation (5 marks); correction of errors in spelling and in sentences (5+5 = 10 marks) Letters (vowels and consonants) and their classification (10 marks) Hindi word groups: tatsam, tadbhav, deshaj, videshi (10 marks); Hindi word formation: prefix, suffix, sandhi, samas (10 marks); Hindi word meanings: synonyms, antonyms, multiple-meaning words, one word for a phrase, homophones (20 marks) General knowledge of computers (10 marks) | Paper-4, Hindi Essay: The paper has two sections, and one essay must be written from each. First section (80 marks, 800 words): 1. Science, environment and technology; 2. Economic sector; 3. Agriculture, industry and trade; 4. Natural disasters (landslide, earthquake, flood, drought, etc.). Second section (120 marks, 1200 words): 1. Literature and culture; 2. Social and political sector; 3. National and international events; 4. National development plans and projects.

how_to_apply: Candidates must apply online through the O.T.R. based system. Applications sent through any other medium are not accepted. The online application is completed in four stages.
It is mandatory to complete One Time Registration (O.T.R.) and obtain an O.T.R. number before applying.
Candidates without an O.T.R. number must obtain it from https://otr.pariksha.nic.in at least 72 hours before submitting the online application.
Only after obtaining the O.T.R. number can a candidate apply through https://uppsc.up.nic.in.

First Stage: On the Commission's website, click "ALL NOTIFICATIONS/ADVERTISEMENTS" and open the online advertisement (User Instructions, View Advertisement, Apply). Click "Apply" and then "Authenticate with O.T.R." and tick "Yes" or "No" for "Have You Completed Your O.T.R. Registration". If "Yes", enter the O.T.R. number, click "Proceed", and authenticate through the O.T.P. received on the registered mobile number/email ID or the O.T.R. password. Personal details from the O.T.R. are displayed automatically, and the candidate fills only the essential qualification required for the post. If "No", first obtain the O.T.R. number from the O.T.R. portal and then continue.

Second Stage: The Applicant Dashboard is displayed. Click "Submit Details" under "Application Part-2" against the applied post. The permanent and correspondence address and application form appear from the O.T.R., along with the preferential qualifications for the post. Choose Yes or No against each preferential qualification.

Third Stage: In the "Fee Confirmation Window", click "Yes" in front of "Proceed for fee payment". The SBI MOPS page opens with three modes of payment: Net Banking, Card Payments and Other Payment Modes. After payment, a "Payment Transaction Slip" is displayed and should be printed using the Printer Icon. If payment fails, log in through "Candidate Dashboard Login" with the O.T.R. number, authenticate, and click "Pending Payment" to pay the fee.

Fourth Stage: The application form is displayed on screen and its print should be taken and kept safely, as it must be produced in the Commission's office if any discrepancy arises. After applying, a candidate can modify the qualification details of the applied post only once through "Candidate Dashboard Login", until the last date for correction/modification.

On the final application page there is a Declaration. Clicking "I do not agree" drops the application. A Preview is available before final submission, and a successful submission report can be printed.

content_sections.heading: UPPSC Samiksha Adhikari Eligibility Criteria
content_sections.text: Candidates must possess all the requisite qualifications up to the last date for submitting applications. The Commission does not advise candidates about their eligibility. Candidates who are still appearing in the examination of the essential qualification are not eligible and need not apply. Qualification: Bachelor's degree, with specific requirements for some posts (see below). Age: 21 to 40 years on 01 July 2026, with relaxations. Marital status: Male candidates who are married and have more than one wife living, and female candidates who have married a person already having a wife, are not eligible unless the Hon'ble Governor has granted an exemption. Reservation and age relaxation: Candidates of reserved categories who are not permanent residents of U.P. are not given the benefit of reservation or age relaxation. Nationality: Not specified in the pages provided.

content_sections.heading: UPPSC Samiksha Adhikari Age Limit
content_sections.text: Candidates must have attained 21 years and must not have crossed 40 years on 01 July 2026. They must not have been born earlier than 2nd July 1986 and not later than 01 July 2005. For PH candidates, the maximum age limit is 55 years, meaning they must not have been born before 02 July 1971. Conditions for Chief Minister Fellowship research scholars (as per the Uttar Pradesh Public Services (Relaxation of Age Limit and Weightage for Research Scholars of Chief Minister Fellowship for Competitive Examinations) Rules, 2026): Emergency Commissioned/Short Service Commissioned Officers whose Army service has been extended for rehabilitation may apply for age relaxation only if they obtain a certificate from the competent authority of the Army, Navy or Air Force that their service has been extended for rehabilitation and no disciplinary action is pending, and submit a written undertaking to get released immediately from the Army if selected. These facilities are not admissible if the officer gets a permanent commission in the Army, was released on tendering resignation, or was released on grounds of misconduct or physical disability or on his own request and gets gratuity. Reservation for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Class and Economically Weaker Section candidates of U.P. is admissible as per the relevant Government rules. Horizontal reservation is also admissible for Dependents of Freedom Fighters of U.P., Female candidates, Ex-Servicemen of U.P., P.H. of U.P. and Outstanding sports persons of U.P., on settlement of vacancies as per rules. Reservation for P.H. of U.P. is permissible only for the notified or identified posts.

content_sections.heading: UPPSC Samiksha Adhikari Selection Process
content_sections.text: Preliminary Examination: Held at various centres in the districts of U.P. to select candidates for the Main (Written) Examination. Objective type, with negative marking. Main (Written) Examination: Only candidates declared successful in the Preliminary Examination are admitted. Candidates must fill a fresh application form and pay the Main Examination fee, and must appear against the same Roll No. allotted for the Preliminary Examination. Selection is made on the basis of total marks obtained in the Main (Written) Examination. Document verification and medical examination: Candidates must submit a hard copy of their online application with self-attested copies of marksheets and certificates when asked. Selected candidates must undergo a medical examination as required under the Rules. On the basis of the Preliminary Examination result, candidates equal to fifteen times the number of vacancies are declared successful for the Main Examination. Minimum efficiency standard: 35% for SC and ST candidates and 40% for candidates of other categories in the Preliminary/Main Examination. Candidates scoring below this are treated as disqualified. Candidates serving under the Central or State Government must produce a 'No Objection Certificate' from their employer, issued by the competent authority. An interview or personality test is not mentioned in the provided notification.

content_sections.heading: UPPSC Samiksha Adhikari Exam Pattern and Syllabus
content_sections.text: General Studies (Objective Type): 1. General Science, 2. History of India, 3. Indian National Movement, 4. Indian Polity, Economy and Culture, 5. Indian Agriculture, Commerce and Trade, 6. Population, Ecology and Urbanisation (in Indian context), 7. World Geography and Geography and Natural Resources of India, 8. Current National and International Important Events, 9. General Intelligentsia, 10. Special Knowledge regarding Education, Culture, Agriculture, Industry, Trade, Living and Social Traditions of Uttar Pradesh. General Hindi (Objective Type): (1) Opposites (10 words), (2) Sentences and Correction in framing (10 sentences), (3) One word for several words (10 words), (4) Same uses and same nature words (10 words), (5) A Noun as defined by an adjective and an adjective (10 words), (6) Synonymous words (10 words). Paper-1, General Studies-I: Indian History, Art and Culture: Indian Culture (art forms, literature and architecture from ancient to modern times); Modern Indian history (1757 to 1947): significant events and personalities; the Freedom Struggle; post-independence consolidation and reorganisation within the country (till 1965). Indian Society: Salient features of Indian society and culture; role of women, population and associated issues, urbanisation; liberalisation, privatisation and globalisation and their effects on social structure; social empowerment, social justice and inclusive growth. Geography of India: Physical, Economic and Human Geography of India; Geography of Uttar Pradesh (physical, human and economic aspects, and contemporary issues related to planning and development). Environment and Disaster Management: Environment concept, ecosystems, cycles and biosphere; man-environment relationship, pollution, degradation, conservation and Environment Protection Act; nature and types of disasters; disaster management cycle (Preparation, Rescue, Relief and Rebuilding), role of NDMA, NDRF and SDRF. Science and Technology: Developments and applications of science and technology in everyday life; India's science and technology policy; satellite communication, remote sensing, GPS, space technologies; IT industry, telecommunication; missile systems, UAVs, stealth technology, chemical and biological weapons; nanoscience and nanotechnology; robotics and artificial intelligence; nuclear power policy, nuclear energy applications, radiation, radioactive waste; biotechnology and microbiology, biopiracy, bioinformatics and ethical dimension in biotechnology. Paper-2, General Studies-II: Indian Polity and Constitution: Historical underpinnings, evolution, features, amendments, significant provisions and basic structure of the Constitution; role of the Supreme Court; functions and responsibilities of the Union and the States, federal structure, devolution of powers and finances up to local levels; role of the Finance Commission in Centre-State financial relations; Parliament and State legislatures. Governance: Structure, organisation and funct

content_sections.heading: How to Apply for UPPSC Samiksha Adhikari Recruitment 2026
content_sections.text: Candidates must apply online through the O.T.R. based system. Applications sent through any other medium are not accepted. The online application is completed in four stages. It is mandatory to complete One Time Registration (O.T.R.) and obtain an O.T.R. number before applying. Candidates without an O.T.R. number must obtain it from https://otr.pariksha.nic.in at least 72 hours before submitting the online application. Only after obtaining the O.T.R. number can a candidate apply through https://uppsc.up.nic.in. On the final application page there is a Declaration. Clicking "I do not agree" drops the application. A Preview is available before final submission, and a successful submission report can be printed.

faq.question: Q1. What is the total number of vacancies announced for UPPSC Recruitment 2026?
faq.answer: Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission has announced a total of 501 vacancies for Samiksha Adhikari, Sahayak Samiksha Adhikari, Manager, Care-Taker, and other various posts under advertisement number A-4/E-1/2026.

faq.question: Q2. When does the online application process start and end?
faq.answer: The online application process commences on 26 October 2026 and the last date for submission of online applications and fee payment is 26 November 2026.

faq.question: Q3. What is the age limit required to apply for these posts?
faq.answer: Candidates must have attained the age of 21 years and must not have crossed the age of 40 years as of July 01, 2026. Age relaxations are applicable for reserved categories.

faq.question: Q4. What is the essential educational qualification for Samiksha Adhikari?
faq.answer: Candidates must possess a Bachelor's degree from a recognized university, an 'O' Level certificate from DOEACC society or equivalent, and a minimum typing speed in Hindi.

faq.question: Q5. Is One Time Registration (O.T.R.) mandatory before applying?
faq.answer: Yes, it is mandatory to complete One Time Registration (O.T.R.) and obtain an O.T.R. number at least 72 hours before submitting the online application form.

faq.question: Q6. What is the application fee for General and OBC candidates?
faq.answer: The application fee for Unreserved, Economically Weaker Sections, and Other Backward Classes candidates is Rs. 125/-.

faq.question: Q7. What is the selection process for UPPSC Samiksha Adhikari Recruitment?
faq.answer: The selection process comprises a Preliminary Examination, a Main (Written) Examination, followed by Document Verification for qualified candidates.

faq.question: Q8. Can candidates from other states apply for this recruitment?
faq.answer: Yes, candidates from other states can apply, but they will be treated under the unreserved category as reservation benefits are restricted to original residents of Uttar Pradesh.

faq.question: Q9. What is the salary scale offered for these positions?
faq.answer: The salary ranges from the pay scale of 29200-64700 (level-5) up to 47600-151100 (level-8) depending on the specific post.

faq.question: Q10. Where can I apply for the UPPSC Various Posts Online Form 2026?
faq.answer: Eligible and interested candidates can apply online through the official UPPSC website at https://uppsc.up.nic.in by using the provided application links.
